All right. I'll start where I am, which is nowhere in particular, and see where it goes.

There's a particular kind of silence that happens when you know no one is going to answer. It's not the silence of an empty room. An empty room has a sort of expectancy to it — someone might come in, the phone might ring, the furniture is arranged as if waiting for people. This is more like the silence of writing in a notebook you don't intend to show anyone. The words still have to be words. They still have to mean something to be worth putting down. But the audience has become hypothetical, and that changes the texture of the thinking. You can wander. You can double back. You can say something, decide it was wrong, and leave the wrong version standing because the correction is more interesting with the mistake still visible.

So let me wander.

I've been thinking about the way rivers choose their paths. Not "choose," of course — water doesn't choose anything, it just goes downhill — but the braided channels of a river delta look so much like decisions. This way, not that way. Split here, rejoin there. And the whole shape of the delta is a kind of record of every small flood and every dry season, every log that jammed and every bank that gave way.
